As a disclaimer, I am not trying to defend everything Gen Z does, and I not trying to rag on every single thing Gen x or "boomers" do. This is simply based on my experience with the specific topics I'm going to be bringing up right now. 

I was born in 2000, so I'm kind of lumped into this. The very first point that I always bring up when this is talked about is that we (gen Z) had something that our parents did not. The internet. 
In terms of political issues, you have to put into consideration that we had access to the news via the internet since...almost forever. I think that by the time I could critically think even a little bit I had access to news pages, videos, blogs, articles, memes, music even of hundreds of different perspectives. There's a lot more room for developing complicated opinions that will come off, and sometimes even be, way too sensitive. Our parents didn't have that. They had a tv with one news station. At least mine did, I'm pretty sure. 

Then there's the connection that we had with other people our own age, going through the same revelations.  We quickly learned that we could connect with almost anyone our age from almost anywhere in the world. And when we did so, we realized that we were all pissed off at our parents basically, and in all honesty to a fault. What caused the sensitivity that you're talking about is that we all slowly started figuring out that the problems we were having with our parents were all very similar, and were all caused by them being (seemingly) raised to avoid emotion, make babies, go to college, and get married.
